answer: No. Texas uses electronic titles, so the title is a record at the state, not a paper document. Your lender sends the lien release to the state electronically, and we transfer the title electronically at your appointment, so you don't need to bring a paper title or a paper release. If the lien still hasn't been released, ask your lender to release it. If that doesn't work, you can sign our lien release request (form NW-LRL-1) and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. We can still make you an offer and book your appointment while you wait.
